pieces.name: main_2story
pieces.notes: 2-story main block, ridge E-W. LiDAR puts the crest (z 32) along the bright line at y 578 with north faces y 515-560 and south faces y 600-620; the image shows the lit 7413 face above that line and a very dark hip-shaped band below it (y 585-670). Read the band as the south face of this hip; the fitter should trust LiDAR for the crest position.

pieces.name: south_block
pieces.notes: second E-W hip south of the trough at y 655-675. LiDAR has north-facing faces z 24-25 at y 696-704 and flats z 20 at the trough. The lit face runs to a clear fascia line at y 750; the trace stops at 717 and is short on this side.

pieces.name: north_wing
pieces.notes: strip north of the trace: roof texture with lit hip-end triangles at the NW and NE corners, vents at y 497, dark middle. Outside the LiDAR mask, so it is either a lower 1-story wing in the main block's shadow or a dark patio cover. Low confidence; drop if no LiDAR.

exclude_notes: ground shadow south of the eave at y 750
tree line east of the house
AC pads and side yard west
notes: Two parallel E-W hips (main 2-story, then a south block) with a trough between them, plus a dark strip of roof north of the trace. Confidence LOW: the image lighting is inverted relative to the LiDAR normals (north faces lit, south faces very dark, shadows both north and south of the house), so I cannot confirm the crest positions by eye; the trace also misses roof at both the north (to y 450) and south (to y 750) ends. Rectangles follow the visible fascia lines; LiDAR should decide the heights.
